MA4344 overview

MA4344 Topic Guide

Cosets and Normal Subgroups

Use cosets to count, and normality to form quotients.

Purpose

Prove left/right coset facts and deploy the high-yield index-2 normality argument.Exam use: Coset side, partition/count, normality criterion, counterexample element and quotient permission are explicit.

Question plan

  1. Write the relevant left and right cosets.
  2. Use the coset equivalence criterion or a bijection to count.
  3. For normality, prove gH=Hg for every g, or use a kernel/index argument.
  4. Only form G/H after normality is established.
  5. Question interpretation: For cosets, prove equality/disjointness before counting; for normality, use a correct equivalent test; for quotient, verify normality before multiplying cosets.

Key terms

gH, Hg, index, normal subgroup H◃G, quotient group. Left and right cosets have equal cardinality; in a finite group their numbers agree.Rapid recall: Left cosets partition G and each has |H| elements; H normal iff gH=Hg for all g iff gHg^{-1}=H; every index-2 subgroup is normal.

Proof method

If [G:H]=2, there are just H and G\H as left cosets, and just H and G\H as right cosets. Thus gH=Hg for each g, so H is normal.Exam workflow: Start from a nonempty intersection to prove two cosets equal, apply the partition to get Lagrange, and use the smallest suitable normality criterion.

Worked simple proof

Claim: every subgroup H of index 2 is normal. If g∈H then gH=H=Hg. If g∉H, both gH and Hg are the unique coset other than H, hence equal.

Practice 1 — index two forces normality [8 marks]

Prompt. Prove that a subgroup H of index two in G is normal. Question-demand diagnosis. The proof needs equality of left and right cosets for every g. Fastest route. Separate g∈H from g∉H and use uniqueness of the sole non-H coset. Topic-specific trap. A subgroup of another small index is not automatically normal.

Prove index 2 implies normal. There are exactly two left cosets: H and GH; likewise the right cosets are H and GH. For g in H, gH=H=Hg. For g notin H, both gH and Hg are the unique non-H coset GH. Hence gH=Hg for every g and H is normal.

Graduated exam bridge

1. List the left cosets of 2Z in Z. Check: 2Z and 1+2Z.

2. Let H≤G and |G|=30, |H|=15. Prove H◃G and state |G/H|. Check: index 2; quotient has order 2.

Practice 2 — left/right cosets in S3 [8 marks]

Prompt. For H={e,(12)}≤S3, list a contrasting left and right coset and decide normality. Question-demand diagnosis. One explicit mismatch proves non-normality. Fastest route. Multiply (13) on the chosen side of both elements of H. Topic-specific trap. Preserve permutation-composition convention consistently when identifying (123) and (132).

Paper-style synthesis: in S3 let H={<e>,(12)}. List left and right cosets and decide normality. Check (13)H={(13),(123)} while H(13)={(13),(132)}, so H is not normal despite having order 2.

Mistakes

  • Treating left and right cosets as equal without normality.
  • Writing a quotient by a non-normal subgroup.
  • Assuming a subgroup of any small index is normal.
  • Recovery rule: A subgroup of order 2 need not be normal; the automatic theorem is index 2.

Checklist

  • I can use aH=bH iff b−1a∈H.
  • I can prove index 2 implies normal.
  • I can separate coset counting from quotient construction.
  • Final 60-second audit: Coset side, partition/count, normality criterion, counterexample element and quotient permission are explicit.
